title: Cotton fingerless mitts
subtitle: Light fingerless mitts in cotton DK for warm-weather wear.
excerpt: Plain fingerless mitts in cotton DK worked in 1x1 rib with a gusseted thumb. Cotton is non-elastic; the pattern compensates with a slightly larger needle and a firmer cast-on count. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Plain ribbed fingerless mitts in cotton DK with adjustments for the lower elasticity of cotton yarn. Construction synthesised from standard fingerless mitt sources with cotton-specific gauge and needle size notes.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts x 26 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 4 mm needles. Cotton gauges looser than wool at the same needle size.

glossaryTerms.definition: A wedge of extra stitches added gradually to build the thumb opening. Gusset increases run along both sides of a marker, matching the natural widening of the hand. The gusset stitches are placed on hold while the hand is completed, then worked separately for the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Plain fingerless mitts in cotton DK, worked in 1x1 rib in the round with a
thumb gusset
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Cotton yarn has almost no elasticity compared to wool. Two adjustments offset this: the needle size is one size larger (4 mm rather than the 3.75 mm used for most DK wool patterns), and the rib is 1x1 throughout to maximise horizontal stretch. The finished mitts are cool, washable, and useful for wearing in spring and summer. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 75 g (160 m / 175 yards) per pair. Cotton is heavier than wool at the same yardage, so weigh the ball before buying.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 75 g (about 160 m / 175 yards) of DK-weight cotton or cotton-blend yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the thumb gusset

items.name: Scrap yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn to hold gusset stitches

content.text: Notes on cotton

items.name: Gauge difference
items.qty: Cotton is inelastic. Swatch on the same needles and yarn you plan to use. Your gauge may differ by 1 to 2 stitches from a wool swatch.

items.name: Thumb bind-off
items.qty: Use a stretchy bind-off such as the k2tog bind-off rather than a standard cast-off. Cotton does not stretch to recover the way wool does.

items.name: Washing
items.qty: Cotton is machine-washable at 30°C. Do not tumble dry; the fabric stretches when wet and should be reshaped while damp.

content.text: Gauge
20 stitches and 26 rounds to 10 cm in 1x1 rib slightly stretched on 4 mm needles. Swatch in cotton specifically; do not rely on a wool swatch.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 1x1 rib for 22 (24, 26) rounds. The cuff measures about 8 (9, 10) cm.
Thumb gusset

Set up gusset: work 1x1 rib to last 3 stitches of the palm, PM, k1, PM, rib to end. Gusset increase round: rib to marker, SM, M1L, work to next marker, M1R, SM, rib to end. Work 2 plain rib rounds. Repeat increase every 3rd round 4 (5, 5) more times. The gusset holds 11 (13, 13) stitches. Work 2 plain rib rounds.
Place gusset on hold and work hand

Thread 11 (13, 13) gusset stitches onto scrap yarn. Cast on 2 stitches over the gap using the backward-loop cast-on. Continue in 1x1 rib until the hand measures 6 (7, 7) cm from the cast-on edge of the gusset bridge. Bind off in rib using a stretchy k2tog bind-off.
Thumb
Return 11 (13, 13) held gusset stitches to needles. Pick up 2 stitches from the gap cast-on. Work 8 (10, 10) rounds of 1x1 rib. Bind off using a stretchy k2tog bind-off.
Common faults
Mitts feel stiff: cotton does not have the drape of wool and needs to be worn in slightly. Washing once before wearing softens the fabric.
Bind-off is too tight to go over the knuckles: work the bind-off on a needle one size larger, or use the k2tog stretchy method.
Thumb hole gaps: cotton has no memory to close gaps naturally. Pick up 1 extra stitch on each side of the gap and decrease away on the first round.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Cotton tails may need a small knot in addition to weaving, as cotton has less grip than wool.
Care
Machine wash at 30°C or hand wash in cool water. Do not tumble dry. Reshape while damp and lay flat to dry.
What to try next

Cotton-linen blends have a similar structure to pure cotton but with a crisper handle and slightly more body. The same pattern works for any DK non-elastic fibre using the same 4 mm needle and 20-stitch gauge.
